author: Abbie Burke
title: 2014 Cold Case closed after FOX21 News story leads to tip - NewsBreak
text:
By Abbie Burke ,
10 hours ago
(COLORADO SPRINGS) — Three years ago, the Colorado Springs Police Department (CSPD) opened its Cold Case Files in hopes of closing some of them for good. FOX21 News highlighted several cases with known suspects that police have been unable to find. One of those stories led to a tip, and eventually the closure of a 12-year-old case.
Jan. 28, 2014; it was a Tuesday morning, just after 7 a.m., when Colorado Springs Police received a call saying there was a dead man in the parking lot of the El Vecino Apartments off South Circle Drive and Monterey Road in the southeast part of the city.
Courtesy: FOX21 News “The Colorado Springs Police Department received a call for service referencing a male lying behind a dumpster, deceased,” said Detective Tracey Thompson, with CSPD.
He was identified as 29-year-old Efrain Murillo Mejia, and according to CSPD, he had been stabbed multiple times.
PREVIOUS COVERAGE: Where is Efrain Murillo Mejia’s killer? “Throughout the investigation, numerous interviews, all the things that we did for the investigation, we were able to identify a suspect: Hermis Pineda Lara,” said Thompson.
An arrest warrant was issued for First-Degree Murder, but an arrest never came.
Courtesy: FOX21 News “Unfortunately, we got information that he fled the country, specifically to Honduras,” said Thompson.
In 2023, FOX21 aired Murillo Mejia’s story in hopes of helping CSPD receive new information on Pineda Lara’s location. “The partnership between the media, FOX21 specifically, has been great, and so we appreciate that,” said Thompson.
After the story aired, Thompson received a tip. “We had a call come in, which I took, and it told us that Mr. Pineda Lara had died in Honduras.”
It took years of legwork and verification through multiple government agencies, but eventually CSPD was able to confirm that Pineda Lara had, in fact, died.
“We were able to get all that paperwork to verify that,” said Thompson. “We presented it to the District Attorney’s office, and they agreed that, because of his death, the case would be closed.”
Courtesy: FOX21 News Detective Thompson said that while she would prefer to see a case brought to court, closing one, regardless of the reason, still feels good. “Not just because it’s a number, but because it’s some type of resolution for the family,” she said.
CSPD has around 120 open cold cases, and investigators said new information is crucial to solving these mysteries.
“People out there know about cold cases and may have information that they think might not be significant or important,” said Thompson. “If you have information, please come forward. There are things that we don’t know that somebody might have that is the key to the puzzle.”
Anyone with information about a cold case is encouraged to call CSPD at (719) 444-7000. Tips can also be made anonymously to Crime Stoppers at (719) 634-STOP.
“That is truly anonymous,” said Thompson. “It is not by name; it is by number, and it is truly anonymous.”
Detective Thompson said this case gives other families waiting for answers hope.
Courtesy: FOX21 News “It means that it could happen,” she said. “It means that there are people out there who have information that could come forward.”
“I’m hoping that with all our cold cases, we get to the point where we clear our arrest warrant cases, identify our homicide suspects, and get a resolution of arrest and justice for the family.”
At the time of his death, Murillo Mejia had lived in Colorado Springs for several years and left behind a wife and a son. A motive for his killing is not known.
